# Matched SFT and DPO training still loses to a simple prior

## TL;DR
We ran matched SFT and factual-label DPO on real Hillstrom data and SmolLM2-135M: 64 GPU updates, four weight reloads, and 35 independent checks. Every trained arm improved Brier over the base but lost to a training-only population prior.

![Matched post-training results](/assets/research/manager-sft-dpo-matched-2026-11-26.svg)

Figure: identical 256-case real-data holdout.

| Arm | Brier | AUC |
|---|---:|---:|
| Train prior | 0.100586 | 0.500000 |
| Base | 0.291316 | 0.384779 |
| SFT 42 | 0.149760 | 0.340270 |
| SFT 43 | 0.150091 | 0.338903 |
| DPO 42 | 0.133842 | 0.348321 |
| DPO 43 | 0.134634 | 0.344068 |

## Methods
Sample 128/256 cases from the frozen disjoint train/test split. LoRA rank4 alpha8 q/v, 230400 trainable parameters, lr2e-4, 16 updates per arm, seeds42/43, MPS fp32. Initial token boundary assertion failed before training; corrected to the canonical trailing-space prompt. DPO pairs factual correct and incorrect digits, not human preference or counterfactual treatment effects.

The prior predicts 13/128, yielding Brier 0.100586 and AUC 0.5. All trained arms have lower AUC than the base. No promotion; no independent blind dataset, full-scale study or sequential SFT-then-DPO comparison.
